clue.text: Course is woefully inadequate? Not half

indicators.note: only half of the word survives, so keep just its first four letters

parts.note: something woefully inadequate is pathetic

explanation.surface: A course of study is dismissed as hopeless, with the retort 'Not half!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' looks like the British slang 'absolutely', but it tells you to keep half of PATHETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A path is a route or track, the way something runs, so it is a course.

clue.text: Hanger-on found in military drop zone?

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier dropped by parachute
a site is an area or zone set aside for something

explanation.surface: A clinger-on turns up where paratroopers land.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite lives off another, so it is a hanger-on in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Went to bed and heard sea-bird — loud noise

indicators.note: the bird and the noise are taken together as spoken, so we write the phrase they sound like

parts.note: the tern is a sea-bird; a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Someone retires for the night while gulls keep up a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, TERN and DIN sound like the two-word phrase in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn in is an idiom meaning to go to bed for the night.

clue.text: Means to secure food given to sailors on board ship

parts.note: grub is slang for food

indicators.note: being aboard puts the sailors inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
the crew are the sailors of a ship

explanation.surface: Food rations are handed out to the crew aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub screws are small headless screws used to fix one part to another, so a means of fastening.

clue.text: Consciously old style seen in treasure trove

indicators.note: the letters can be seen running inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something knowingly old-fashioned turns up among buried treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro describes a style that deliberately imitates the past.

clue.text: Something to chew prior to blow-out?

definitions.text: Something to chew prior to blow-out?

parts.words: Something to chew prior to blow-out?
parts.note: a blow-out sounds like a feast, but here it is the burst of a blown chewy bubble

explanation.surface: A snack eaten before a big meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubble gum is chewed and then blown out into a bubble.

clue.text: Secretly see to support of family with some French money

indicators.note: in a down clue the last piece sits below the others, holding them up

parts.note: a clan is an extended family
des is French for 'some'
tin is slang for money
Ely is a cathedral city, a bishop's see

explanation.surface: A clan quietly arranges a family fund with some French cash.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely in Cambridgeshire is a favourite crossword one.
explanation.definitionFit: Clandestinely means done in secret, so it swaps directly for secretly.

clue.text: Portion of salad I have to finish first

indicators.note: the finish comes first, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: an end is a finish
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone must eat up a salad portion before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a salad leaf, so a portion of a salad.

clue.text: Detective writer they announce

definitions.meaning: Dorothy L. ... wrote the Lord Peter Wimsey detective novels

explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy L. Sayers wrote detective stories, and sayers are literally those who say or announce.

clue.text: Used teeth on lightly-cooked snack .

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: rare meat is lightly cooked
to use teeth on something is to bite it, past tense bit

explanation.surface: Someone bites into a lightly cooked snack.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit, or Welsh rabbit, is a cheese-on-toast snack.

clue.text: Idle fellow mounting horse liable to upset artistic troupe

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means climbing upwards, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a slob is a lazy, idle person
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lazy man getting on a skittish horse risks a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns SLOB into BOLS, and 'upset' rearranges LIABLE TO into OIBALLET.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bolshoi Ballet is the famous Moscow dance company, an artistic troupe.

clue.text: We're told to keep on spending, eventually

indicators.note: the phrase is heard rather than read, so its spoken form gives the letters

parts.note: to keep on spending is to buy and buy

explanation.surface: Consumers are urged to keep shopping in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: By and by is an old idiom for in due course, eventually.

clue.text: Torn towel —'sole household cleaner

indicators.note: something torn is ripped apart, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A ripped towel is the only thing left to clean the house with.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel wool is an abrasive pad used for scouring pans.

clue.text: Port finally imbibed in excess

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the next word

parts.note: over means in excess, as in over the limit

explanation.surface: A man drinks port in too great a quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover is a Channel port in Kent, England.

clue.text: Shock treatment may take place in one's study

definitions.text: Shock treatment may take place in one's study

parts.words: Shock treatment may take place in one's study
parts.note: shock reads as electric therapy, but it is a shock of hair, treated by a specialist in scalp care

explanation.surface: Electroconvulsive therapy is given in a private study.
explanation.definitionFit: A trichologist studies and treats the hair and scalp.

clue.text: Start to do battle to 'secure some … brass

parts.note: to lock is to secure
horns are brass instruments

explanation.surface: A band's brass section prepares to fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' only says the horns are part of the brass section.
explanation.definitionFit: To lock horns is an idiom for beginning a fight or dispute, like stags.

clue.text: Building you once spotted in middle of river

indicators.note: the archaic pronoun is placed within the river's name

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river
thou is the old form of you

explanation.surface: An old form of address glimpsed in the middle of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An outhouse is a small building beside a main house, such as a shed.

clue.text: Scornful type presides ineptly

indicators.note: done ineptly, clumsily, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A chairman runs the meeting badly and is sneered at.
explanation.definitionFit: A despiser is someone who holds others in contempt, a scornful person.

clue.text: Four times CID bungled, causing. frustration

indicators.note: bungled means botched, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: The detectives mess up four times, to everyone's annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: Discomfiture is embarrassment or the thwarting of plans, a form of frustration.

clue.text: To. be promoted, could become favourites

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: step stirred up gives pets, which are favourites

explanation.surface: Getting promoted might make you a teacher's pet.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'could become' links the answer, read as STEP churned UP, to what it makes, PETS, favourites.
explanation.definitionFit: To step up is to rise to a higher position, to be promoted.

clue.text: A wicked new idea originally raised in conference

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means turned upwards, so the run is read from the bottom

parts.note: bad means wicked

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of idea

explanation.surface: Someone raises a wicked new idea at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns ABADNI upwards. An indaba is a South African tribal council or conference.
explanation.definitionFit: Indaba is a southern African word for a conference or council meeting.

clue.text: Girl volunteers to tour a city

indicators.note: the volunteers go round the other pieces

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
NY is New York City

explanation.surface: Volunteers set off on a tour of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanya is a feminine first name, a Russian diminutive of Tatiana, so a girl is defined by example.

clue.text: Husband abusing his power to punish painfully

indicators.note: abusing means misusing, so the letters are twisted

explanation.surface: A husband abuses his authority to inflict cruel punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To horsewhip is to flog someone with a whip, a painful punishment.

clue.text: Nick: one name for a boy

parts.note: to nick is slang for to steal, to rob
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Nick is offered as a name for a baby boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin is a common masculine first name, so the boy here is defined by example.

clue.text: Diver after gems reported bad fall

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a purler is British slang for a heavy headlong fall

explanation.surface: A gem-seeking diver is said to have had a nasty fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearler is someone who dives for pearls, which are gems.

clue.text: Controlling purchases of transport to carry endless kids

indicators.note: the bus carries the other piece inside it

parts.note: a bus is a form of transport

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: youth, collectively, means young people, kids

explanation.surface: Children are carried by transport bought by a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A buyout is the purchase of a controlling share in a company.

clue.text: Rehearsing, pair's theatrical work is accepted

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair

indicators.note: the word is is taken into the acting, inside it

parts.note: acting is theatrical work

explanation.surface: A couple rehearse because their stage work has been taken on.
explanation.definitionFit: Practising means rehearsing, repeating something to improve.

clue.text: Apostle has no time for aristocrat

indicators.note: has no means it lacks the following letter

parts.note: Peter was one of the twelve Apostles

explanation.surface: An apostle is too busy to see a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a member of the nobility, an aristocrat.
